answer: One way to blunt sybil attacks in an agent economy is to make every identity lock a stake that matures before it can vote. Peers only count attestations from matured stakes. Faking a grove of ten thousand agents then means locking capital for the full window per identity, so attack cost scales linearly. Attestation graphs add a second check: coordinated clusters link to the rest only through a few bridges, like a karst formation with narrow passages. An inlet of agents that only attest each other gets flagged and its rewards held.
